requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`.

**Item kinds and names**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys]` outlines a YAML source and asserts each item's selector and line span.
- Block mapping entries come out as `pair` items named by their written key: `pair[a]`, and `pair["b"]` with its quotes kept.
- A flow mapping entry `c: {d: 1}` yields a nested `pair[d]`.
- Block sequence entries come out as anonymous `item@` nodes: `item@` and `item@/pair[f]` appear in the asserted summary, and a scalar entry `- 2` is also an `item@`.

**Nesting and spans**
- The same test asserts nesting under the nearest enclosing item, such as `pair["b"]/pair[e]/item@/pair[f]`.
- It also asserts line spans, including a leading comment run: `# c` is owned by `pair[a]`, whose span is `1-2`.
- Multi-line parents such as `pair["b"]` (`3-7`) end at their last non-comment token.

**Owned comments in the span**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry]` checks that a trailing comment is included in the entry's text and span.
- It checks that a preceding comment is included in `pair[d]`'s selection (`# before next\nd: 2`).
- It checks that `pair[a]` stops at its last non-comment token, which excludes that following comment. It also checks `pair[a]/pair[b]`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` checks that a comment between sibling keys belongs to the following key (`pair[jobs]/pair[second]`) and not to the previous one.

**Cited requirements**
- Comment ownership and selector grammar are cited, not owned, by this requirement. Their own tests cover them, for example `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language`.
- Selector and percent-encoding behavior also appears in `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits`.

**Residual points**
- Flow sequences are not listed as items. A supplementary test, `language_name_spans_retain_original_bytes_when_selectors_are_normalized`, uses `key: [1]` and expects only `key`. It has no `{test}` reference to this requirement, but it adds no uncovered obligation.
- I found no obligation without a test, no wrong expected result, and no acknowledgments to weigh.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
